samples.summary: A transient resolve failure evicts a working shared session (unmounts the Yorkie document), because `error` is preferred over still-valid cached `resolved`
samples.evidence: `if (!token || error || !resolved)` at line 1124 renders "Link unavailable" whenever the query is in an error state, even though react-query keeps the last successful `data` in `resolved`. With `retry: 1` (two attempts, ~1s apart) any short API/network outage during a background `refetchInterval`/focus refetch flips the branch, unmounting `SharedDocumentInner` and with it `YorkieProvider`/`DocumentProvider` — detaching the document, destroying editor/undo state and any not-yet-synced local edits, and (per the comment at lines 945-948, `useViewAnalytics` "exactly one session per visit") double-counting a view when it recovers up to 60s later. The comment claims "a single network blip does not evict a working session", but two back-to-back attempts over ~1 second is a single blip. A background failure should not discard data that resolved successfully; only a definitive 401/404/410 (revocation/expiry) should.

samples.summary: Making `resolved.role` live breaks the explicit "role is fixed for the route lifetime" assumption in slides-view and notes-view: an editor→viewer downgrade never reaches those editors
samples.evidence: This delta makes `resolved` (and hence `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"`, shared-document.tsx:383/460) change mid-session. docs-view and board-view list `readOnly` in their effect deps and rebuild, but slides-view.tsx:1222-1228 excludes `readOnlyMount` with the comment "it is derived from a share-link role that is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario", and notes-view.tsx:157 has deps `[didMount, doc]` with `readOnly` only consumed at `initialize(...)` (line 138). After a downgrade, a shared slides/notes session keeps a fully writable editor over a document whose link is now viewer-only — the exact hole this change sets out to close, left open for two of the five document types, and now on a path that actually fires.
searchedFor: grep readOnly in slides-view.tsx / notes-view.tsx / board-view.tsx
read effect dependency arrays of each view

samples.summary: `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` in the import path is never disposed, leaving the constructor's `doc.subscribe` attached across `client.detach(doc)`
samples.evidence: Line 224 constructs a store purely to call `setDocument` and drops it; the store's constructor subscription (yorkie-doc-store.ts:633) is never released, unlike the sibling board branch which does `store.dispose()` in a `finally` (lines 229-236) precisely because "the store subscribes to the doc in its constructor". Now that `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` exists, this is the one remaining unreleased subscription; impact is bounded (the document is detached right after and is not long-lived), but the callback still holds the doc alive and mirrors the leak this change fixes elsewhere.

samples.summary: Polling continues indefinitely after the view has already collapsed to the "Link unavailable" page
samples.evidence: `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` is unconditional, so a permanently revoked/expired token keeps issuing one resolve request per minute per open tab from a page that shows only an error, forever. Passing a function form that returns `false` once the query has errored with a definitive status would stop it.

finding.summary: A transient resolve failure evicts a working shared session (unmounts the Yorkie document), because `error` is preferred over still-valid cached `resolved`
finding.evidence: `if (!token || error || !resolved)` at line 1124 renders "Link unavailable" whenever the query is in an error state, even though react-query keeps the last successful `data` in `resolved`. With `retry: 1` (two attempts, ~1s apart) any short API/network outage during a background `refetchInterval`/focus refetch flips the branch, unmounting `SharedDocumentInner` and with it `YorkieProvider`/`DocumentProvider` — detaching the document, destroying editor/undo state and any not-yet-synced local edits, and (per the comment at lines 945-948, `useViewAnalytics` "exactly one session per visit") double-counting a view when it recovers up to 60s later. verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as claimed: shared-document.tsx:1124 is `if (!token || error || !resolved)`, preferring the query `error` over still-valid cached `resolved`. The query (lines 1106-1118) has refetchInterval 60s (SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS at line 87), refetchOnWindowFocus, staleTime 0 and retry:1 — so two failed attempts ~1s apart during a background/focus refetch flip the branch. With @tanstack/react-query ^5.74.4 (package.json:56), a failed refetch after a prior success sets `error` while `data` (i.e. `resolved`) is retained, so the "Link unavailable" screen renders despite valid cached data. resolveShareLink (api/share-links.ts:99-111) rejects on any network failure or non-OK status, not just 401/404/410, so transient outages qualify. Taking the branch replaces SharedDocumentInner (line 1138), unmounting YorkieProvider/DocumentProvider (lines 1003-1076) — detaching the Yorkie document and discarding editor/undo state and unsynced local edits — and remount re-fires useViewAnalytics, which the comment at 945-948 says must record exactly one session per visit. No guard elsewhere distinguishes transient from definitive failures. Real error-handling / data-loss bug in the correctness lane; major.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. shared-document.tsx:1106-1118 makes `resolved` live (refetchInterval 60s per line 87, refetchOnWindowFocus, staleTime 0), and its own comment (1090-1105) states the goal is that an editor→viewer downgrade tightens authority mid-session. `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` is computed at shared-document.tsx:383 (notes) and :460 (slides) and forwarded to NotesView (417) and SlidesView (552)/MobileSlidesView (676). However slides-view.tsx consumes `readOnlyMount` (:198) only inside the mount effect (:722, :753, :1074, :1077) whose deps are `[didMount, doc]` (:1228), with an explicit comment at :1222-1226 excluding `readOnlyMount` because the role "is fixed for the lifetime of the route". notes-view.tsx passes `readOnly` to `initialize(...)` at :138 with deps `[didMount, doc]` at :157 and never re-applies it (later effects at :177/:184/:189 only handle theme/viewMode/keymap). By contrast docs-view.tsx:590 has deps `[didMount, doc, readOnly]` and its comment at :578-585 says `readOnly` is load-bearing because initialize() captures it once — confirming the asymmetry. Nothing remounts the editors: the DocumentProvider docKey (shared-document.tsx:992-1001) depends only on documentId/type, so `doc` identity is stable across a role change and neither effect re-runs. Per shared-document.tsx:1094-1096 the client-side readOnly is the real write boundary under the default YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false. Result: after a downgrade, shared slides and notes sessions keep a fully writable editor — a stale-state/broken-invariant correctness bug on a path this change actively creates. No guard found that makes it unreachable.
